title: Kenyan Indigenous Games Board games
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Creative Arts and Sports; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts and Sports teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Boards can be pits in the ground or carved wood; seeds or pebbles as counters. Game names are for a teacher to confirm.

skills.key_step: The child names indigenous board games (bao and other sowing games), says how a turn is played (sow one seed per pit, capture) and what they build.

floor.question: What happens when a runner is tagged?

representations: a bao board or pits in the ground
steps: Pick up the seeds from a pit.
Sow one into each pit in turn.
contexts: a break-time game under a tree

board.do: Where does the last seed land?

misconceptions.ask: Which is an indigenous Kenyan board game?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a chess board with a bao board of pits.

misconceptions.ask: Does winning at bao depend only on luck?
misconceptions.repair: Play a round and plan two moves ahead.

misconceptions.ask: Name a benefit of indigenous board games.
misconceptions.repair: List what the mind does in one game.

misconceptions.ask: When sowing in bao, how many seeds go in each pit?
misconceptions.repair: Sow slowly, counting one per pit.

checks.question: Name a benefit of board games.
checks.answer: any of: counting, planning, patience, mental health
